themes_detail.label: Lead contamination spike
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints in CD 205 surged to 3 this week versus a baseline of 0.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1100% spike (z-score: 6.35)—marking an urgent public health signal in a district with significant housing stock that may contain legacy lead hazards.
evidence: 3 lead complaints filed this week vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1100% increase, z-score 6.35)
Lead is a neurotoxin with no safe exposure level; children under 6 are at highest risk
CD 205 (Fordham/University Heights) contains older housing stock built before 1978 lead paint ban
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Health to learn which buildings triggered complaints and what remediation occurred
Interview residents with children in affected buildings about testing and exposure risks
Investigate whether contractor activity or demolitions (257 DOB permits filed recently) disturbed lead paint

themes_detail.label: Encampment and homelessness crisis
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 19 this week compared to a 5.0 weekly average over 8 weeks (280% increase, z-score: 3.21), while homeless assistance requests spiked to 6 this week versus 1.9 baseline (220% increase), suggesting a rapid deterioration in street homelessness across the district.
evidence: 19 encampment complaints filed this week vs. 5.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (280% spike, z-score 3.21)
6 homeless person assistance requests this week vs. 1.9 weekly baseline (220% spike, z-score 2.84)
Community Board repeatedly requests 'other programs to address public health issues' but pattern suggests unmet service gaps
reporting_angles: Map encampment locations this week; interview outreach teams about capacity constraints and service gaps
Speak with residents near encampments about quality-of-life impacts and city response times
Investigate whether recent cold weather or policy changes in nearby districts drove migration to CD 205

themes_detail.label: Illegal street vending surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped to 13 this week versus a 3.2 weekly average over 8 weeks (300% spike, z-score: 3.26), indicating either a rapid increase in unlicensed street vending activity or heightened resident frustration with enforcement.
evidence: 13 vendor enforcement complaints this week vs. 3.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (300% increase, z-score 3.26)
No recent Reddit or local news mentions, suggesting this is a hyper-local 311-driven signal
Aligns with community budget requests for 'more sanitation' resources, suggesting sidewalk/street quality concerns
reporting_angles: Identify specific blocks or corridors where vendors are concentrated; photograph and document activity
Interview Department of Consumer Affairs about whether vending licenses in the district are declining and enforcement is lagging
Talk to street vendors about whether economic hardship or policy changes drove uptick in unlicensed activity

themes_detail.label: Building code violations uptick
themes_detail.summary: Building/Use complaints spiked 3 weeks ago to 9 versus a 2.5 weekly baseline (260% increase, z-score: 4.6), coinciding with 257 active DOB permits filed recently (138 alterations, 77 new buildings), suggesting renovation and construction activity may be triggering code compliance issues.
evidence: 9 building/use complaints filed 3 weeks ago vs. 2.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (260% spike, z-score 4.6)
257 DOB permits filed in last 90 days, including 138 alterations and 77 new buildings
Related spikes: sidewalk condition complaints up 167% last week (5 vs. 1.9 avg), suggesting construction debris impacts
reporting_angles: Cross-reference DOB permits with building/use complaint addresses to identify problem projects
Interview Department of Buildings about whether inspection capacity is adequate for current construction volume
Document impacts on residents—noise, dust, sidewalk obstruction—from active construction sites

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints jumped to 5 last week versus a 1.9 weekly average over 8 weeks (167% increase, z-score: 3.37), a signal that may be linked to recent construction activity and deferred street maintenance documented in repeated community budget requests for sanitation resources.
evidence: 5 sidewalk condition complaints last week vs. 1.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (167% increase, z-score 3.37)
Community Board has filed recurring requests for 'more sanitation trucks and equipment' year after year
257 active DOB permits (many for alterations) may be contributing to sidewalk damage and debris
reporting_angles: Walk the district and photograph worst sidewalk conditions; cross-reference complaint locations with DOB permit sites
Interview Department of Sanitation about maintenance schedules and resource allocation in CD 205
Determine whether construction activity or deferred maintenance is the primary driver of deterioration
